transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Orchid - Lead ML Eng), Ava Torres (Orchid - Platform SRE), Liam Chen (Orchid - Security)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. we can do a quick agenda — walkthrough of console tracing, dig into request logs and error analysis, and then do a short Q&A. sound good?
[00:20] Samir: yep thanks, we mainly want to see the debugging flow end-to-end — how we triage a bad response and tie it back to prompts, model versions, and infra. and security questions too.
[00:35] Priya: awesome. quick note, i'll be demo-ing from the staging tenant so some names look different, but the features map 1:1 to prod. i'll share my screen now.
[01:10] Priya: okay opening the Console — top nav, tracing tab. we show per-request traces that include route, model version, latency breakdown (tokenization, network, GPU), and the KV cache hit rate. you can filter by model, route, status code, and custom tags like customer-id.
[02:12] Ava: that filter UI looks handy. can we pin a filter set for our team? we have multiple services hitting the API.
[02:30] Priya: yep, we have saved views and team-level dashboards. you can also annotate traces — e.g., mark a trace as "regression" which ties into rollouts.
[03:05] Jordan: quick product context — tracing is integrated with request logs, so you can open a trace and jump to the raw request/response payload and metadata. this is helpful when you need to see the prompt + model output together with infra-level metrics.
[04:00] Samir: how accurate is the tokenization breakdown? sometimes our prompts have lots of unicode and tokens look off.
[04:20] Priya: good call — tokenization is the same tokenizer we use in the runtime; it's possible some special chars get collapsed differently, and the console shows both the tokenized sequence and the token count. if you want i can show an example with a messy prompt.
[05:30] Priya: demo: i trigger a request that returns an unexpected hallucination, show trace, then open request logs. timestamp, request-id, model, model-version, route, and route metadata appear at top.
[06:15] Priya: here you can see the call stack — client region, assigned GPU node (if dedicated), and queue wait time. note that in hosted mode the node is abstract but we still show latency buckets.
[07:02] Liam: we need audit logs for compliance — can the request logs be exported and do they include redaction options?
[07:25] Priya: yes — exports to S3 or as a CSV. we support field-level redaction for PII before export, and you can define retention policies per route. for private deployments we also support customer-managed KMS for encrypting logs at rest.
[08:10] Jordan: to add, we have an API for pulling logs programmatically so your SIEM can ingest them.
[09:05] Samir: what about SSO and role-based access? we don't want devs to see production payloads.
[09:25] Priya: we integrate with SAML/SSO and have granular RBAC. you can scope permissions to routes, environments, and limit who can view raw payloads. there's also an "redacted view" toggle.
[10:05] Priya: switching to error analysis tab — we automatically group errors by signature (e.g., OOM, timeout, model-error, bad-output flagged by eval hooks). you can click a group to see examples and related traces.
[11:00] Ava: does grouping happen client-side or during ingest?
[11:15] Priya: a mix — ingest pipeline annotates error type, then grouping logic in the service clusters similar stack traces and model responses. you can add custom rules to change sensitivity.
[12:30] Priya: demo: here's a canary rollout where the new quantized model shows a spike in "bad output" classification for a specific prompt set. we can rollback or route that traffic to a fallback model automatically.
[13:15] Samir: how do we configure the fallback? per-route?
[13:35] Priya: per-route, yes — in the routing policy you can set fallback model variants, tiers (hosted vs dedicated), and region fallback. fallbacks are first-class in the console.
[14:40] Jordan: question for you Samir — what's your success criteria for a pilot? throughput, latency SLO, cost per 1k tokens?
[15:05] Samir: latency 95th under 400ms for short prompts, and sustained throughput of ~200 rps during peak, cost needs to be competitive with our current infra.
[15:30] Priya: noted. we can run a short benchmark with your sample workload to show latencies and cost projections with batching and KV cache.
[16:10] Priya: back to request logs — you can search by request-id, user-id, or correlation id. we also support log-linking to external tracing systems (jaeger, datadog) by adding a correlation header.
[17:05] Ava: timezone and regional logs — we operate EU and US regions; can we ensure logs for EU traffic stay in EU?
[17:30] Priya: yes, we support region-aware retention and storage. in Private deployments you can strictly keep logs in-region. for hosted we have regional tenants that can be pinned.
[18:40] Priya: now i'll show a live debug: filter for 5xx errors in the last 30 minutes, open a trace that shows a spike in model queue wait time, then inspect request payload. you can replay the request to a sandbox model from the console as well.
[19:55] Jordan: replay is useful. is replay recorded as an event in audit logs?
[20:12] Priya: yes, replays are auditable and show who triggered them and the target environment.
[21:00] Samir: our security team will ask about encryption keys. can you confirm KMS integrations?
[21:20] Priya: we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and support HSMs in private deployments. customer-managed keys for logs and model data is supported in Private and Dedicated setups with proper controls.
[22:45] Liam: and for compliance do you surface access logs per user and provide SSO mappings?
[23:00] Priya: yes, access logs, SSO mapper, and we can provide reports for audits. we've got SOC2 and ISO summaries in the security pack Jordan will share.
[24:30] Priya: switching to the diagnostics panel — you can aggregate error rates by prompt template, model version, and route. there's an anomaly detection toggle that notifies when error rates deviate from baseline.
[25:40] Samir: are those alerts via webhook/Slack/email?
[25:55] Priya: all of the above, plus paging integrations. thresholds can be static or adaptive based on historical traffic.
[27:10] Priya: small demo: open a request log row, expand the nested payload — transcription has some artifacts (auto-transcription of audio) so sometimes words are slightly off — console exposes raw and normalized fields.
[28:05] Ava: we've seen mistaken attributions in other tools; how often are traces misattributed?
[28:30] Priya: rare, but attributable to clock skew or missing correlation headers. we recommend adding a unique correlation id from your side; the console will pick it up and surface it.
[30:00] Jordan: quick pause for questions — anything else on the trace/log linkage?
[30:10] Samir: just one: how do we keep our dev team from seeing prod payloads? more on RBAC please.
[30:25] Priya: you can create roles that deny raw payload view, allow aggregated metrics only. also recommend using environment tags and separate projects for prod vs staging.
[31:40] Priya: now debugging flows — typical process we recommend: 1) Identify failing traces via alerts, 2) open sample traces and request logs, 3) examine model/version diffs and prompt/response, 4) check infra metrics (queue, GPU mem), 5) optionally replay in sandbox and create a remediation (rollback or patch).
[33:00] Samir: sounds good. can we export that chain into a ticket in Jira?
[33:20] Priya: yes, integrations for Jira allow you to create a ticket pre-populated with trace links, logs, and suggested remediation steps.
[34:10] Samir: in terms of cost optimization — how does KV caching and batching show up in the console? can we see token savings?
[34:30] Priya: the Optimize tab has charts for cache hit rates, average tokens saved per route, and estimated cost saved. you can simulate different batching policies and see projected cost/latency tradeoffs.
[35:45] Ava: we have a strict requirement to keep request payload retention to 30 days, after which it must be purged. can retention be per-route?
[36:00] Priya: yes per-route retention windows are supported and can be enforced with retention policies; purge jobs are auditable.
[37:20] Jordan: user question — if we go Dedicated, do we still get the same console features?
[37:35] Priya: yes, Dedicated and Private have parity for Console features; with Dedicated you'll see physical node IDs and more infra metadata, and in Private you control the storage and KMS.
[38:50] Samir: one last question from security: do you redact embeddings or are they stored raw?
[39:10] Priya: embeddings can be redacted or encrypted at rest; we also support not storing embeddings if you set that policy.
[40:05] Jordan: ok wrapping up — quick recap and next steps. we'll send the security pack (SOC2/ISO), run a short benchmark with your sample workload, and schedule pilot kickoff next week.
[41:15] Samir: thanks, that's helpful. will follow up on sample traffic and RBAC mapping.
[42:00] Ava: please include a quick how-to for setting up SAML + RBAC in the docs you send.
[42:30] Jordan: noted. Priya any final notes?
[42:40] Priya: i'll include a short video clip of the debug flow and the bench script we use.
[43:00] Liam: thanks all.
[43:20] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll email the pack and schedule. talk soon.

Meeting end.

References / Links mentioned: Security pack (link in follow-up), benchmark script (to be shared), sample dashboard screenshot (shared during demo).

Note: transcription has occasional small errors — e.g., product names may be slightly off or spelled differently in the raw transcript.
